land.text: the whole Han empire as the last Western Han emperors left it (Cliopatria's Han shape of 36 BC to 5 AD, 4.47 M km2, which its first Xin shape repeats within 11 cells)

predecessors.note: 'Wang usurped the throne and officially proclaimed the Xin' (Xin page); 'Wang Mang proclaimed emperor: 10 January 9' (infobox). Cliopatria starts the Xin row in 6, at Emperor Ping's death (3 February 6 AD, Han page), when Wang Mang was regent, three years before the proclamation. The colour registry already puts Xin in the Han's colour group.

land.text: the Xin's last shape, taken by the Gengshi Emperor's restored Han when Chang'an fell on 5 October 23

successors.note: Xin page infobox: 'Succeeded by Eastern Han and Chengjia' (garbled); 'In 25 AD, Liu Xiu was crowned as Emperor Guangwu of Han in Luoyang'. The Wang Mang page: the Gengshi Emperor 'took the throne in 23 and was deposed by the Red Eyebrows'. The han-dynasty dossier carries the Gengshi regime and Guangwu's Han as the same state.

capitals.name: Chang'an (Xi'an)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Chang'an'. Wang Mang page: Chang'an ('eternal peace') 'was redesignated Chang'an 常安; constant peace'. Sacked on 4 or 5 October 23. Han Chang'an lies in the north-west of modern Xi'an.

rulers.name: Wang Mang
rulers.title: emperor (Xin)
rulers.note: Wang Mang page: reign AD 9-23; 'The rebels sacked the capital on 4 October 23'; 'Died: 6 October AD 23 (aged 67) Chang'an.' He was regent for the child emperors of the Han before 9; the Xin page dates his proclamation 10 January 9.

correction.text: the 14 shape (without the Tarim, Dzungaria, Turfan and Fergana) plus the Hexi Corridor; holds 9-13

keyframe_review.note: 4,465,527 km2 (19,242 grid cells), the whole Han empire, for 6-13. Two corrections. Years: the Xin begins on 10 January 9 (infobox), not 6; Emperor Ping died on 3 February 6 AD (Han page) and Wang Mang only 'cemented his control' (Xin page) until the proclamation, so 6-8 stays with the Han (han-dynasty keyframe) and this shape holds 9-13. Land: the Tarim Basin, Dzungaria, Turfan and the Fergana edge (2,419 cells) are not Xin land: 'The post [of protector-general] was abandoned after the usurpation of Wang Mang (Xin dynasty) from 8 to 22 CE' (Protectorate page) and 'The troubles for Xin with the Xiyu kingdoms started in AD 10' (Wang Mang page). Cliopatria itself removes them in 14, which is also the shape used here, plus the Hexi Corridor (433 cells) that Cliopatria drops at 14 for no reason any page gives: no page opened says Hexi left the Xin (inference from silence, flagged). Area check: the Han page's infobox gives 6.0 M km2 for 50 BC and 6.5 M for 100 AD; 4.47 M is 0.74 of the 50 BC figure, within a factor of two. The Xin page gives no area.

correction.text: the 14 shape plus the Hexi Corridor; holds 14-22, with the rebel-held land of 17-22 handled by the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 3,659,104 km2 (16,393 cells) for 14-22: the empire without the Tarim and Hexi. Hexi (433 cells) is put back for the reason given at xin-dynasty_6. The Western Regions are right to be absent: 'during the civil war the Protectorate of the Western Regions was overrun by the Xiongnu' (Xin page); in the year 16 'Wang's renewed attempt failed and one army was cut off at Qiuzi' (Wang Mang page). From about 17 'several rebellions began' (Wang Mang page): the Lülin in Hubei and the Chimei hold ground that the page does not name; see the ledger's placeholders.

correction.text: unchanged, for 23 only (to 5 October 23); 24-29 pass to the han-dynasty dossier

keyframe_review.note: 2,466,380 km2 (11,016 cells): Cliopatria removes Shandong (830 cells), Henan (689), Hubei (364), Hunan, the south and the southwest by 23, which fits a civil war that 'Xin armies were completely defeated by Han restorationist armies in the Battle of Kunyang in June-July 23 AD' (Xin page) came to decide, but no page names the lost lands. The shape stands for 23 only: 'Chang'an captured: 5 October 23 AD' ends the Xin. Cliopatria keeps the Xin label to 29; 24-29 are the Gengshi regime, Guangwu's Han, the Chimei and the Sichuan and Gansu warlords (han-dynasty keyframes).

region.text: the whole Xiongnu state, Huhanye's tributary realm

ledger.note: 9: the Xiongnu stay Wang Mang's tributary. Wang Mang page: his envoys 'exchanged the Xiongnu seal for one that changed Xiongnu to Gongnu', implying vassal status, 'before AD 10' with no date. The tie begins with the Han (53 BC, han-dynasty ledger) and passes to the Xin unchanged.

region.text: the Han empire, taken over by Wang Mang

ledger.note: 9: Wang Mang proclaims the Xin at Chang'an. 'Wang Mang proclaimed emperor: 10 January 9'; 'Wang usurped the throne and officially proclaimed the Xin'. The Wang Mang page has only 'the winter of 8 CE' and AD 9-23 for the reign. The land is the whole Han empire.

10: Wang Mang breaks with the Xiongnu. 'Wang, irritated, declared war against Xiongnu' after the seal affair; the Xin page: the Xiongnu 'intended to intervene in China around 10/11 AD' and Wang responded 'by mobilizing 300,000 soldiers along the northern border'. The xiongnu dossier (ia-01) has the matching vassal_end in 10. Reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19): source moved to the Xin page, which gives the year ('around 10/11 AD'); the Wang Mang page gives none ('sometime before AD 10').

region.text: Hubei, where the Lülin bands rose

ledger.note: About 17: the Lülin rebel in Hubei. 'two insurgent bands in Hubei were recruited by Han loyalists' and became known as the Lulin (Xin page); 'About AD 17, as the burdens from the wars and the corruption continued to increase and famines occurred, several rebellions began' (Wang Mang page). Year and province are the pages'; the Xin page says 'large-scale civil war by 19 AD'. Reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19): source moved to the Wang Mang page, which gives the year ('About AD 17') and the place ('Lülin rebels in modern Yichang, Hubei'); the Xin page gives no year.

region.text: 'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu' (Wang Mang page): a 150 km disc round Linyi and a 100 km disc round Xuzhou, limited to the cells the Xin held in 14 and no longer in 23 (432 cells)

ledger.note: About 17: the Chimei rise in southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu. The Wang Mang page names the Chimei with the Lülin among the rebellions 'about AD 17' and says they 'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu', and has Wang targeting 'the Chimei' first in 22; the Xin page says the Red Eyebrows were 'defeated by Liu Xiu's forces in 27 AD'. Year and place are the page's, the outline is the researcher's reading. Reviewer ea-02-c (2026-10-19) replaced the earlier Shandong, Henan and Hubei placeholder (Hubei is the Lülin's land).

23: the Xin falls to the rebels. 'Chang'an captured: 5 October 23 AD'; the Xin armies were 'completely defeated by Han restorationist armies in the Battle of Kunyang in June-July 23 AD'; the Wang Mang page: 'in early 23, Liu Xuan was proclaimed the Gengshi Emperor' and 'The rebels sacked the capital on 4 October 23'.

region.text: 'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu' (Wang Mang page): a 150 km disc round Linyi and a 100 km disc round Xuzhou, limited to the cells the Xin held in 14 and no longer in 23 (432 cells)

ledger.note: 23: the Xin ends with the Chimei still undefeated in southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu; they go on to take Guanzhong from the Gengshi regime (Guangwu page) and surrender in 27. Region as in /ledger/4 (reviewer fix 2026-10-19).

region.text: the Xin's last territory: Guanzhong, the north and the west

ledger.note: 23: Chang'an falls and Wang Mang is killed. 'The rebels captured Chang'an in October 23, plundering the capital and killing Wang Mang'; Wang Mang died 6 October 23. What is left of the Xin goes to the Gengshi Emperor's restored Han, which the Wang Mang page has deposed by the Red Eyebrows and the Guangwu page succeeded in 25.
23: the Xin dynasty ends with Wang Mang's death. 'Chang'an captured: 5 October 23 AD'; 'By 37 AD, the Han dynasty was fully restored.'

wars.name: Wang Mang's war with the Xiongnu
wars.outcome: Wang Mang declared war after the seal dispute and mobilised 300,000 soldiers along the northern border with a plan of twelve armies; no page opened names ground taken or lost. Chanyu Zhi died in 13.
wars.note: The Xin page dates the intervention 'around 10/11 AD'; the end year here is the chanyu's death in 13, the only later date on the Wang Mang page. The xiongnu dossier carries the Xiongnu side.

wars.name: Lülin and Chimei rebellions (fall of the Xin)

union.text: Hubei, the Lülin's land ('in modern Yichang, Hubei', Wang Mang page)

'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu' (Wang Mang page): a 150 km disc round Linyi and a 100 km disc round Xuzhou, limited to the cells the Xin held in 14 and no longer in 23 (432 cells)

zones.text: the Lülin's Hubei and the Chimei's southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu

wars.outcome: Rebellions from about 17 became a civil war by 19; the Lülin forces, with the Gengshi Emperor proclaimed in early 23, beat the Xin at Kunyang in June-July 23 and took Chang'an on 4-5 October; Wang Mang was killed on 6 October.
wars.note: The Wang Mang page adds that in 22 'the Lülin forces suffered the effects of a major plague which killed about half of the rebels' and that Wang attacked the Chimei first. Zones: Hubei for the Lülin, southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu for the Chimei ('roved through large swaths of territory', Wang Mang page); reviewer fix 2026-10-19.

certainty.note: The Xin inherited the Han frontiers; the steppe, Tarim and southern frontiers are approximate and the rebel-held lands from 17 have no named boundaries.

sources.title: Xin dynasty
sources.note: Proclaimed 10 January 9; Chang'an captured 5 October 23; Xiongnu war 10/11; Kunyang 23; no area figure. Thin.

sources.title: Wang Mang
sources.note: Accession, Chang'an renamed Chang'an (constant peace), Xiongnu seal change, Western Regions troubles from 10 and 16, rebellions about 17, Gengshi Emperor early 23, Chang'an sacked 4 October, death 6 October 23.

sources.title: Protectorate of the Western Regions
sources.note: Founded 59/60 BC (Zheng Ji, Wulei), abandoned under Wang Mang (8 to 22), Chen Mu 74, Ban Chao 91, abandoned 29 July 107, restored 123-124 by Ban Yong. Thin on seats and extent.

sources.title: Han dynasty
sources.note: Identity, dates, capitals, infobox areas (50 BC 6.0 M km2, 100 AD 6.5 M km2), Emperor Wu's annexations of Nanyue (111) and Dian (109), the Commanderies of 108, Hexi 121, the Protectorate 60 BC, Xin 9, Guangwu 25, Qiang 107-118, warlords, abdication December 220.

notes: Cliopatria's three Xin shapes are kept as adjusted. (1) The row starts in 6 at Wang Mang's regency; the Xin is proclaimed on 10 January 9 (infobox), so 6-8 passes to the han-dynasty dossier (Emperor Ping died 3 February 6 AD, Han page). (2) The row runs to 29 but the Xin ends on 5 October 23 (infobox 'Chang'an captured'); 24-29 are the Gengshi, Guangwu and warlord years. (3) The Tarim, Dzungaria, Turfan and the Fergana edge are removed from the 6 shape (Cliopatria removes them at 14); Hexi is added back to 14 (inference from silence). ONE STATE OR TWO: the colour registry groups the Xin with the Han (same colour) and Cliopatria has separate rows; this dossier is its own state, with han-dynasty both predecessor and successor, so the compiler can draw either way. Pages opened: Xin dynasty, Wang Mang (2 of 1-2); the Protectorate and Han pages are cited from the han-dynasty research (read for that dossier) for the Tarim withdrawal and the area comparison. THIN PAGES: the Xin page gives no area, no capital history, no date for the Western Regions' loss and no places for the Lülin or Chimei beyond 'Hubei'; the Wang Mang page is silent on Goguryeo's year, the Dian rebellion, the provinces and the Chimei's land. The Chimei and Lülin have no Cliopatria row and no dossier: they are written as rebel dossiers in this group (lulin, chimei) from the same pages, with a placeholder region; 'Gengshi regime' is carried inside han-dynasty. Not on any page: Wang Mang's eastern capital at Luoyang, the 12 AD Goguryeo revolt, the Yellow River flood's territorial effect, the Dian/Yizhou uprisings.
